headline: Brentford without two midfielders, and the market keeps it close
summary: Brentford are 6th in the Premier League with 10 points and host a Nottingham Forest side on 3 straight defeats. But Brentford must rebuild their midfield: Janelt and Yarmolyuk were both sent off in the 1-2 home defeat to Liverpool and are suspended. Forest's position hides a better attacking story — they average 1.72 expected goals a game, more than Brentford's 1.27, and The New York Times reports Gibbs-White and Milenkovic should be fit. That is why the market makes Brentford only about half a goal the better side at home, at 47.3% to win across the bookmakers, margin removed. The fair goals total is 2.72.
read: Brentford are sixth and at home, but the market has them only half a goal better than a Forest side on three straight defeats, with both Brentford midfielders sent off against Liverpool suspended. Forest create more than they concede and have won three of the last five meetings, which is why the goals line sits squarely on 2.75 and the away price holds at 27.8%.

facts.fact: Yehor Yarmolyuk and Vitaly Janelt were both sent off in the second half of Brentford's 1-2 home defeat to Liverpool and are suspended for this match.
facts.meaning: Brentford must rebuild the middle of the team that has carried them to sixth.

facts.fact: Brentford are the favourites at 47.3% to win, against Nottingham Forest's 27.8%.
facts.meaning: The home side is favoured but short of a coin flip, with the draw at 24.9% very much live.

facts.fact: Nottingham Forest have lost their last three Premier League games: 0-1 to Arsenal, 1-3 at Crystal Palace and 0-1 to Coventry.
facts.meaning: One win in seven and 19th in the table — this is a side under real pressure going to a top-six ground.

facts.fact: Forest average 1.72 xG per game across their last five, more than Brentford's 1.27.
facts.meaning: Forest are creating more than the team they face, despite scoring only three goals in those five matches.

facts.fact: Brentford are sixth with 10 points from seven games, unbeaten in four of their last five (LDWWD).
facts.meaning: A strong start built on results rather than dominance — the top-six position is what makes them favourites here.

facts.fact: Morgan Gibbs-White is reported fit and Nikola Milenkovic should also be available for Forest's next Premier League game.
facts.meaning: Forest's key creator and their first-choice centre-back in contention strengthens the case for the away side.

facts.fact: The handicap fair line is -0.41 goals in Brentford's favour, with the main line at -0.5.
facts.meaning: The market sees Brentford as less than half a goal better on their own pitch — a near-even game with home advantage as the tiebreak.

facts.fact: The market's fair goal total is 2.72, with the main line at 2.75 and the over at 49.3%.
